original_value: We study stream reasoning in datalogMTL—an extension of Datalog with metric temporal operators. We propose a sound and complete stream reasoning algorithm that is applicable to a fragment datalogMTLFP of datalogMTL, in which propagation of derived information towards past time points is precluded. Memory consumption in our algorithm depends both on the properties of the rule set and the input data stream; in particular, it depends on the distances between timestamps occurring in data. This is undesirable since these distances can be very small, in which case the algorithm may require large amounts of memory. To address this issue, we propose a second algorithm, where the size of the required memory becomes independent on the timestamps in the data at the expense of disallowing punctual intervals in the rule set. Finally, we provide tight bounds to the data complexity of standard query answering in datalogMTLFP without punctual intervals in rules, which yield a new PSPACE lower bound to the data complexity of the full datalogMTL.

result.paraphrase: We investigate stream reasoning in datalogMTL, an extension of Datalog that includes metric temporal operators. We present a sound and complete stream reasoning algorithm for the datalogMTLFP fragment of datalogMTL, where derived information is not propagated to earlier time points. The algorithm’s memory use depends on both the rule set and the input stream, especially on the gaps between timestamps in the data. This is problematic because these gaps may be very small, causing the algorithm to need substantial memory. To remedy this, we introduce a second algorithm whose memory requirements are independent of the data timestamps, but it forbids punctual intervals in the rule set. We also establish tight data-complexity bounds for standard query answering in datalogMTLFP without punctual rule intervals, which imply a new PSPACE lower bound for the data complexity of full datalogMTL.
